text:
oncall-bot: 🔔 Alert: Incident 824 14 Partial VPC Peering / PrivateConnect degradation for customer 'CoralPay' in eu-west-3. Symptoms: DNS NXDOMAINs to private hostnames, intermittent connection blackholes to peered subnets, spikes in TCP retransmits. Paging network + SRE.

net_eli: ack. seeing a bunch of withdrawn prefixes reappearing from peer-az and some routes being learned via customer-router then via our peering. looks like a leaking import-policy from customer side or duplicate advertisement.

sre_maya: can you paste BGP neighbor summary and any recent route-change counts? also any negative-cache events on our private-dns?

net_eli: quick snippets:
```
BGP neighbor 198.51.100.2    Established 00:21:10  prefixes 12/0
Neighbor 198.51.100.3 flaps: 23 in last 15m
Route 10.99.0.0/16 via 198.51.100.2 (local-pref 100)
Route 10.99.0.0/16 via 198.51.100.3 (local-pref 100)
RIB updates: 10.99.0.0/16 withdrawn 14 times
```

net_eli: negative caching events on our private DNS resolver show NXDOMAIN cached for `svc-auth.coralpay.internal` at TTL 300 but then a sudden SRV/ A appear, clients hit cache leading to auth failures.

eng_rox: pulled logs from resolver cluster and the PrivateLink endpoint. dig shows intermittent no-answer responses during flaps: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> svc-auth.coralpay.internal @10.0.2.5
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; SERVER: 10.0.2.5#53(10.0.2.5) (UDP)
```

ops_ivan: CoralPay ops reporting user payments failing intermittently (transaction API 502s) and webhook deliveries delayed. They've opened internal incident CP-879. I'm posting to the customer channel now.

pm_sasha: we need a short impact blurb for status page. note time window and affected services.

sre_maya: mitigation hypothesis: customer advertised their internal 10.99.0.0/16 back into our fabric (route leak) causing traffic to hairpin between AZs and our private-dns consistency to break. Short-term: 1) suppress the duplicate advertisement via route-map deny on peering 2) flush DNS negative cache entries for the affected names 3) nudge client TTLs if possible. Plan to apply (1) immediately.

net_eli: applying route-map to drop adverts of 10.99.0.0/16 from peer 198.51.100.3 (scoped to peering vrf). Applying now.

oncall-bot: change detected by deploy-bot: peering-policy-update/2026-04-02T14:21Z 14 net_eli (apply)

eng_rox: after suppress, BGP stops toggling. route now consistently via 198.51.100.2. DNS queries that hit authoritative resolver start returning answers. Captures show fewer retransmits.

sre_maya: execute DNS negative-cache flush across private resolver fleet for CoralPay zones. eng_rox can you run the flush script?

eng_rox: running `scripts/flush-negcache --zone coralpay.internal --ids resolver-{1,2,3}` 
`OK: flushed 3 shards`

ops_ivan: just posted to CoralPay: "We observed a route leakage from a customer-side router causing intermittent internal DNS NXDOMAINs and partial blackholing. We have suppressed the offending advertisements and flushed resolver caches; services are recovering." customer acked, provided logging showing reduced error rate.

net_eli: continuing to monitor BGP flaps metric: flaps drop to 0 within 90s. route-change rate returns to baseline.

vendor-tac-bot: Opened vendor cases with ProviderX: case PX-120334 — requesting packet capture from peering POP and asking for any smoothing config that might amplify customer-origin adverts.

pm_sasha: timeline note: Impact window 14:20-14:29UTC. Visible effects: payment API 502 spikes, webhook delivery latency; retries mitigated some user-visible failures. I'll draft the status update.

sre_maya: moving to MITIGATED state. net_eli please own the RCA and confirm whether the leak originated customer-side misconfig or a session reflection on our rr. Also verify authoritative resolver cache consistency after flush.

net_eli: taking handoff. immediate follow-ups: request BGP updates from customer (ask them to audit their export policy), run `show route-map` and `show ip bgp regexp` on our reflectors, and validate no accidental community stripping. I'll coordinate with ProviderX TAC.

customer-notify-bot: Sent mitigation update to CoralPay ops channel and attached incident id 824, log extracts, and recommended client backoff tuning for 30s.

eng_rox: attaching digest: pcap-ID PCAP-824-1, resolver-logs-14-21-14-30, bgp-dump-14-22.

pm_sasha: postmortem action items: 1) add automated detection for duplicate prefix advertisements within a tenant VRF, 2) add DNS negative-cache auto-flush when authoritative answers re-appear, 3) update peering runbook to include immediate suppression steps. I'll file tickets.

oncall-bot: Incident 824 status changed: MITIGATED by sre_maya at 2026-04-02T14:31Z — handoff to net_eli for RCA. Please update incident board.
